title: Incident Priority Matrix and Auto-Runbook Invocation Spec
author: Aisha Collins
content:
Overview

This page defines a standardized incident priority matrix and the corresponding automated runbook invocation specification used by Redwood Inference responder tooling. The goal is to reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to restore (MTTR) by ensuring consistent, auditable automation triggers for common severity classes while keeping human escalation paths intact. This doc complements the runbook library and incident evidence standards.

Scope

- Applies to: all production-facing services that contribute to user-visible SLOs (text generation, embeddings, streaming, dedicated capacity routing).
- Excludes: planned maintenance windows; security incident invocations are handled via the Security Incident Response SOP.

Definitions

- Incident signal: any aggregated alert, synthetic failure, or SLO deviation that crosses thresholds in monitoring.
- Auto-runbook invocation: programmatic triggering of a runbook flow (notifications, mitigation scripts, throttles, fallback routing).
- Responder roles: Primary Pager, Secondary Pager, Bridge Operator, Service Owner, Incident Commander.

Priority matrix (summary)

Priority: P0
- Customer Impact: Global outage for hosted API or Dedicated control plane; >95% customers affected
- SLO deviation threshold: Error rate > 5% absolute or latency p95 > 3x target for 5m
- Pager: Platform SRE + Service Owner
- Auto-runbook allowed: Yes
- Suggested automated actions: Route traffic to fallback region; enable degraded tier; open incident bridge; notify sales/CS

Priority: P1
- Customer Impact: Significant region or tenant outage; major customer impact (>5% tenants)
- SLO deviation threshold: Error rate > 2% absolute or latency p95 > 2x target for 10m
- Pager: Service SRE + Primary Pager
- Auto-runbook allowed: Yes
- Suggested automated actions: Isolate noisy nodes; auto-scale dedicated capacity pool; enable model-fallback policy

Priority: P2
- Customer Impact: Partial degradation, elevated errors for subset of traffic
- SLO deviation threshold: 20% increase in error rate or latency percentile regressions over baseline for 30m
- Pager: Primary Pager
- Auto-runbook allowed: Conditional (per runbook)
- Suggested automated actions: Apply cache warm restart; toggle nonessential tracing; raise sampling

Priority: P3
- Customer Impact: Low-impact functional regressions, single-customer issues
- SLO deviation threshold: Localized errors not affecting SLO
- Pager: No page
- Auto-runbook allowed: No
- Suggested automated actions: Create ticket; schedule follow-up; attach debugging traces

Runbook invocation principles

1) Safety first: Automated actions that modify traffic routing, disable models, or issue credits must be guarded by rate limits, circuit breakers, and pre-approval flags associated with the service owner.
2) Visibility: Every auto-invocation creates an immutable incident event with: trigger source (monitoring rule id); timestamp; automation rule id and version; actor (automation-service principal).
3) Idempotence: Automation flows must be idempotent and tolerate repeated invocations for the same incident event id.
4) Graceful escalation: If automation cannot restore within a configurable window, escalate to human oncall and widen the notification fan-out.

Automated invocation lifecycle

- Detect: monitoring -> alert rule evaluates to TRUE.
- Enrich: orchestration service fetches runbook metadata & recent change events for the affected service.
- Evaluate: automation engine runs guard checks (owner flag, blackout windows, incident frequency limits).
- Execute: if guards pass, execute the runbook steps via orchestrator (scripts, API calls, runbooks).
- Observe: collect evidence, post status to bridge and status page, attach logs to incident evidence store.

Detailed example: model-fallback auto-runbook (P1)

Purpose: transparently switch a subset of user requests to a compatible model variant when primary model latency or token errors exceed thresholds.

Preconditions:
- Service owner has enabled auto-fallback for the model family (owner flag = true).
- The model variant catalog contains a validated fallback mapping and compatibility matrix.

Step-by-step (automation):
1) Trigger: monitoring alert 'model-primary-token-error-rate' > 2% for 5 minutes (monitoring rule id: alert-ml-024).
2) Enrich: get recent deploys (gitops commit id), active rollout percentage, and tenant-impact estimate.
3) Guard checks: owner flag = true; no active security incident for model artifacts; recent fallback for same model < 30 minutes? If yes, delay and notify humans.
4) Execute (orchestrator calls): update routing policy to add fallback model with initial weight 20% for 10 minutes; warm cached KV entries for fallback model on target GPU nodes; post status to bridge and status page.
5) Monitor: if error rate improves to baseline within 10 minutes, roll back the fallback. If not, escalate to oncall.

Automation rule spec (human-readable summary):
- automation_rule_id: runbook-fallback-model-2026-v1
- priority: P1
- trigger: monitoring_rule=alert-ml-024; evaluation_window_minutes=5
- guards: owner_flag=true; blackout_windows=[]; recent_fallback_minutes=30
- actions: update-routing (fallback_model_id=model-x-quant-v2; initial_weight_percent=20; duration_minutes=10); cache-warm (nodes=gpu-pool-3); post-status (message='Auto-fallback engaged for Model X (20%)')

Invocation evidence (example fields created on event):
- event_id: evt-20260215-8f3a
- source: monitoring.alert.alert-ml-024
- priority: P1
- service: text-generation-api
- detected_at: 2026-02-15T09:14:06Z
- evidence: slo-latency-p95=2.8s; error-rate=3.1%
- automation_rule_id: runbook-fallback-model-2026-v1

Runbook safety gates and approvals

- Manual override switch (owner-level): boolean flag in the service config to disable auto-runbook invocations for that service. Default = false.
- Emergency stop: global circuit breaker maintained by Platform SRE that halts all auto-invocations for a rolling 10 minute window if systemic conditions are detected.
- Audit log retention: automation events retained for 365 days; exportable for regulatory review.

Escalation timings and human handoff

- If automation executes and the incident is not materially improved within the rule's monitoring window (default 10 minutes), escalate to Primary Pager immediately and add Service Owner to the bridge within 5 minutes.
- If no acknowledgement from a human pager within 2 minutes of escalation, escalate to Secondary Pager and notify SRE lead.
- For P0 incidents, the orchestration also triggers executive-notify channel and the Customer Success on-call list.

Status page and customer communications hooks

- Every auto-invocation must create a status page event draft with templated content including: short summary, affected functions, mitigation steps, and expected restore window.
- Template variables: {service}, {impact}, {mitigation}, {eta}, {next_update}. The automation posts the initial draft and marks it as 'needs-review' for a CS rep to publish if required by customer-facing SLAs.

Operational runbook governance

- All automation rule changes require PRs in the orchestration repo with a code owner review from Platform SRE and the owning service's oncall lead.
- Periodic audits: quarterly smoke tests of top 10 automation rules during game days; results published to the runbook-library audit log.

Game day and testing guidance

- Run automated-rule dry-runs in a synthetic sandbox once per month. Dry-runs must use synthetic-event ids, replay of real traces, and a controlled traffic reroute to avoid customer impact.
- Include one automated-fallback scenario in the annual oncall certification game day.

Ownership and contacts

- Automation policy owner: Platform SRE (team alias: platform-sre@redwood.ai).
- Orchestration repo lead: Oliver Chen.
- Runbook-library maintainer: Marta Gomez.

Appendix: monitoring rule examples and IDs

- alert-ml-024: model-primary-token-error-rate > 2% for 5 minutes (P1 auto-invoke)
- alert-svc-101: api-global-error-rate > 5% for 5 minutes (P0 auto-invoke)
- alert-lat-502: p95-latency > 3x SLO for 5 minutes (P0 escalation)
